evidence.locator: From prompt to pull request; Which models and agents; security FAQ
evidence.finding: Users connect GitHub repositories, choose Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode, submit a prompt and observe cloud work in a browser. The web workflow advertises draft/ready PRs and app-side merge subject to upstream protections. Marketing safety claims are not an independently tested containment result.

evidence.title: Sparkles native CLI installation and authentication
evidence.locator: Prerequisites; macOS/Linux installer; npm and Windows; Verify installation; Start a session
evidence.finding: The CLI runs installed claude, codex or opencode on the local computer. It documents v1.3.0 and a build commit. Each harness retains authentication ownership. Local-only sessions are supported; mirrored sessions require Sparkles login and consent. Platform/channel signing differences are explicit.

evidence.title: Sparkles coding-harness selector
evidence.locator: Choose the active agent; footer; handoff
evidence.finding: The terminal UI selects installed harnesses and restarts into a fresh native local session when switching. Model and reasoning settings are separate. The selector also mentions Grok, but the install/model documentation does not establish its concrete launch/auth route in this bounded pass.

evidence.title: Sparkles local model and account boundary
evidence.locator: Opening and Why a model may be unavailable
evidence.finding: The local harness/provider controls its own authentication, account entitlements and accepted models. Sparkles passes settings to the selected installed runtime; it does not grant provider access. Model names are not extra coding harnesses.

evidence.title: Sparkles non-interactive local commands
evidence.locator: Select values for one run; configuration precedence
evidence.finding: Runtime, model and effort flags also apply to sparkles exec. Repository configuration and environment settings choose defaults while the native harness continues to own credentials. An external CI invocation is not a product-owned scheduler.

evidence.title: Sparkles managed sandbox API quickstart
evidence.locator: Access grant; create; stream; send follow-up; terminate
evidence.finding: Signed-in users create an organization-bound API key, submit repositories and a prompt, then observe an asynchronous managed coding job over authenticated event streams. No API or product was executed during this source pass.

evidence.title: Sparkles sandbox lifecycle and PR contract
evidence.locator: Access model; Lifecycle; Create requests; Files and pull requests
evidence.finding: Sandbox ownership is bound to the exact API access grant, with serialized concurrency checks and lifecycle events. File reads are bounded; agent-driven writes and short-lived repository-scoped GitHub App credentials create or reuse a draft PR. The API contract is narrower than the advertised web draft/ready PR workflow.

evidence.title: Sparkles organization credit pricing
evidence.finding: The page offers 500 credits for $50 per month, annual billing with twelve months of credits paid for ten, and custom Enterprise deployment on customer infrastructure. One credit corresponds to $0.10 of model inference. Only an initial first-organization grant of 100 credits is advertised; no recurring free cloud allowance is established. The dollar currency code is not stated.

evidence.title: Sparkles analytics and replay controls
evidence.locator: Section 9, Cookies and Tracking; Privacy settings
evidence.finding: The policy says optional PostHog analytics and separately optional masked replay can be rejected, customized or withdrawn through Privacy settings in the app or site footer. evidence.finding: The main service provides coding sandboxes and GitHub PR access under account-based terms.
